name: Projected Minimum Degree
definition: The **Projected Minimum Degree** is the maximum, over all coordinate projections of $\mathcal{H}$, of the minimum degree of the projected class's $1$-inclusion graph.
graph_summary: Largest minimum degree among coordinate projections.
origin_references: Minimum degree in one-inclusion graphs, including counterexamples to its proposed VC upper bound, is studied by Rubinstein, Bartlett, and Rubinstein (2007); the projected envelope is the catalogue's p-monotonic construction.

p_monotonic.proof: Every coordinate projection of pi_T(H) is a coordinate projection pi_U(H) of the original class, for some U contained in T. Thus the collection over which the maximum defining the projected minimum degree of pi_T(H) is taken is contained in the collection for H.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is a restriction to a fibre followed by a projection.  It is recorded separately from subfamily monotonicity because the latter has not been established for this maximum-of-minimum-degrees parameter.
